purpose: Held-out validation data for version 1.0 (CLAUDE.md 6.7 item 1, D-061): never used to build, choose or tune the model. Digitised by Claude on 2026-10-12 from NTRS copies in reference/docs/. The ARCAS CP data of TN D-4013 and TN D-4014 were used to choose the transonic fin interpolation (D-056) and are no longer independent; they are kept in wind-tunnel-validation.json and reported separately.

method.pass1: values read by eye against the printed grid from the 250 dpi page renders before the pixel pass (exception: L8A05, see its note)
method.pass2: pixel coordinates of gridlines and of the curve or symbol transcribed from the same renders with a 50 px ruler overlay (or 3x zoomed strips with a 10 px ruler), converted by the axis calibration recorded with each series
method.uncertainty: the larger of half the worst disagreement between passes and the reading floor (0.5 % body length or 0.02 diameters for CP, 0.01 for a force coefficient, 0.15 per radian for C_N_alpha)
method.curve_identity_check: every digitised panel was re-read against its legend and the report text before pass 2: Blue Scout fig 8(a) solid line = fins on (text: C_N_alpha 0.184 per deg at M 0.8 confirms the curve); RM E50D28 fig 8(c) and (d) curves are labelled by angle of attack on the plot; TN 2944 fig 9(b) lower band = 73.25 in models A, B, C, E (legend in the panel), C_D_T above C_D_B; TN D-3182 fig 4(a) and 5(a) symbols by roll angle and tunnel (legend); TM X-1661 fig 4 symbols by fin aspect ratio (legend), fig 2(a) by nose and fin (legend); L8A05 fig 8(a) model A circles (legend)

blue_scout_tn_d_1958.source: NASA TN D-1958 (1963), 1/15-scale Blue Scout model, Langley 8-foot transonic pressure tunnel, Mach 0.60 to 1.03, Reynolds number 3.18e6 to 4.12e6 per foot; configuration D = body + fins, no flare, no protuberances, delta_f = 0 (figure 8(a) PDF page 31, solid 'fins on' curve; figure 5(c) PDF page 21 and 5(d) PDF page 22, circles)
blue_scout_tn_d_1958.reference: coefficients on 0.0388 sq ft (d = 2.67 in); x_cp as a fraction of the overall length 57.72 in (apex to fin trailing edge); moment reference 66.3 % of length

reynolds_per_foot.note: linear in Mach between the two, from the test conditions

cn_alpha_per_deg.note: per degree; the text gives 0.184 per deg at M 0.8 for the fins-on model, which the pass-2 reading reproduces

geometry_inches.note: figure 1(a) (PDF pages 9 to 10): spherical nose tip r = 0.43 on a 22 deg half-angle cone of length 2.56 to diameter 2.06; cylinder 2.06 to station 29.69; conical transition 29.69 to 32.90 from 2.06 to 2.67; cylinder 2.67 to the base at 57.25 (fin trailing edge 0.47 beyond, overall 57.72); four fins: root chord 2.42, tip chord 0.47, exposed span 2.40, leading edge sweep 45 deg, single-wedge section with 8 deg included angle, leading-edge radius 0.017, root leading edge at station 54.76 (wedge thickness at the root trailing edge 2.42 tan 8 deg = 0.34, taken as the mean thickness 0.17 for the drag section 'square')
geometry_inches.modelling: the spherical tip is replaced by the sharp 22 deg cone (apex 0.43/sin(22 deg) - 0.43 = 0.72 in ahead of the sphere centre; the virtual apex is station 0 of the drawing within 0.1 in); the fins' root trailing edge overhangs the base by 0.47 in

rm10_naca_rm_e50d28.source: NACA RM E50D28 (Luidens and Simon 1950), half-scale RM-10 with four fins, Lewis 8 by 6 ft supersonic tunnel, Mach 1.49, 1.59, 1.78, 1.98, Reynolds number 29.1, 29.2, 29.5, 31.1e6 on the body length; figure 8(c) (PDF page 34) centre of pressure against Mach at alpha 2, 4, 6, 7 deg; figure 8(d) (PDF page 35) drag coefficient against Mach at alpha 0 to 7 deg
rm10_naca_rm_e50d28.reference: coefficients on the maximum cross-section (d = 6 in); centre of pressure in diameters ahead of the base (station 73.25 in)

cd_alpha0.note: the plotted lines are straight and Mach independent (the report says so, p. 2); alpha = 2 deg line 0.2565

geometry_inches.note: figure 2 (PDF page 19): parabolic body b = x sqrt(c/2) (2 - x/45), c = 2/15^2, 0 <= x <= 73.25 (maximum diameter 6 at x = 45, base radius 1.818; 0.25 in removed from the nose, overall 73 in); four fins of circular-arc profile, t/c 0.10 normal to the leading edge: leading edge swept 60 deg from the normal at station 64.5, parallelogram planform with streamwise chord 9.07 (4.54 normal to the edges, TN 2944 figure 1 gives 0.0504 L with L = 90), tip at radius 8.95, thickness 0.454; wetted area 1033 sq in, volume 1291 cu in
geometry_inches.modelling: nose = parabolic series K = 1, length 45, radius 3 (the removed 0.25 in tip is kept: 0.3 % of length); boattail = the same parabola continued, which the unclipped parabolic transition (K = 1) of GEO-7 reproduces exactly (b = 3 - u^2/675 for u = x - 45); fins: root chord 9.07 (8.75 on the body, the rest behind the base), tip chord 9.07, sweep 11.86 at the tip, span 6.85 from the mean root radius 2.10, cross-section 'airfoil'

rm10_flight_naca_tn_2944.source: NACA TN 2944 (Evans 1953), compilation; figure 9(b) (PDF page 34): total and base drag coefficient of the 73.25 in free-flight RM-10 models A, B, C, E (magnesium alloy, polished, four fins) against Mach 0.9 to 2.5 at alpha = 0; figure 10 (PDF page 35): Reynolds number on the body length against Mach for each model
rm10_flight_naca_tn_2944.reference: coefficients on the maximum cross-section (d = 6 in); free flight, so the base drag is included in C_D_T

reynolds_on_length.note: figure 10, 73.25 in models: A 20e6 at M 0.93 to 58e6 at 1.5; B 16e6 at 1.0 to 76e6 at 2.0; C and E 15e6 at 1.2 to 78e6 at 2.5; used piecewise: A below 1.5, B 1.5 to 2.0, C/E above 2.0

rm10_flight_naca_tn_2944.geometry: the E50D28 half-scale geometry (73.25 in flight models are the same shape, Table I PDF page 19)

cd_total.note: value series = pass-2 pixel readings (dense in the drag rise); pass 1 compared at its own Mach numbers by interpolating pass 2

cd_base.note: base drag coefficient, single pixel pass, +-0.01: squares at M 1.0 to 1.1 y 1535 px, 1.2 to 1.3 y 1550, 1.5 to 1.9 y 1530, 2.0 to 2.5 y 1535

rm10_flight_naca_tn_2944.caveat: TN 2944 reports unexplained differences between wind-tunnel results with fins attached and flight results (summary): the flight C_D_T is about 0.03 below the 8 by 6 ft tunnel value at Mach 1.5 to 2.0 (figure 13)

tn_d_3182_model_A.source: NASA TN D-3182 (Yuska 1966), one-fifth scale model A of a sounding rocket second stage, Lewis 10 by 10 ft (M 2.0 to 3.47, Re 2.34e6 to 2.49e6 per ft) and 8 by 6 ft (M 1.79 to 2.06, Re 4.9e6 to 5.03e6 per ft) supersonic tunnels; figure 4(a) (PDF page 14): C_N_alpha at zero normal force and centre of pressure against Mach; figure 5(a) (PDF page 15): C_A at zero normal force; Table II (PDF page 8) test conditions
tn_d_3182_model_A.reference: coefficients on the body cross-section (d = 6 in); C_N_alpha per radian; x_cp in calibers from station 0

cn_alpha_per_rad.note: M 2.0 (10 by 10 ft tunnel) is the mean of two circles at zy 708 and 685 (tests 1 and 1A); the squares are the 8 by 6 ft tunnel at the nominal Mach numbers of Table II

x_cp_over_d.note: calibers from station 0 (nose tip), d = 6 in; M 2.0 circles at zy 1470 and 1535 averaged

ca_zero_normal_force.note: axial force at zero normal force, sting mounted with base pressure measured; whether the base term is removed is stated in the report's symbols (C_A, no correction noted)

geometry_inches.note: figure 1 (PDF page 9): nose 25.9 long with the coordinate table (station, radius): (1.143, 0.306), (1.905, 0.449), (3.810, 0.754), (5.714, 1.023), (7.619, 1.278), (9.524, 1.523), (11.428, 1.759), (13.333, 1.986), (15.238, 2.204), (17.143, 2.414), (19.048, 2.614), (20.952, 2.793), (22.857, 2.927), (23.810, 2.970), (24.000, 2.975), (24.762, 2.994), (25.900, 3.000), described in the text as approximately a three-quarter-power nose; cylinder radius 3.0 to station 65.9; four fins of 77.66 sq in total planform (section B): root chord 9.15, tip chord 6.54, exposed span 4.38, leading edge swept 45 deg, thick wedge section of 10 deg included angle with a blunt trailing edge (tip trailing-edge thickness 0.57 = 6.54 tan 5 deg), leading-edge radius 0.1; the fin trailing edge at the base
geometry_inches.modelling: nose = power series fitted to the coordinate table by least maximum error (the exponent is computed and recorded in the model file); fins: root 9.15, tip 6.54, sweep 4.38, span 4.38, thickness 0.69 (mean of the root and tip trailing-edge thicknesses 0.80 and 0.57), cross-section 'square' (blunt base), root leading edge at 56.75; the wedge lift effect that the report adds (its reference 2) is not in Barrowman's method

tm_x_1661_config1.source: NASA TM X-1661 (1968), half-scale ARCAS variants at Mach 2.01, Reynolds number 9.8e6 per metre; figure 4 (PDF page 16): aerodynamic-centre location in percent body length for low angles of attack, configurations 1 (l/d 18.20) and 2 (23.77) with conical, ogive and spherical noses and low (basic) and high aspect ratio fins; figure 2(a) (PDF page 10): C_A against alpha for configuration 1
tm_x_1661_config1.reference: percent of body length from the nose; coefficients on the body cross-section

ca_alpha0_config1.note: figure 2(a) C_A at alpha = 0 for configuration 1, single pixel pass (crop origin (440, 1640) of page 10; C_A = 0.6 - (y - 35)/1170; alpha = 0 at x 344): the low and high aspect ratio curves overlap near alpha = 0, so the symbol identification carries +-0.015
ca_alpha0_config1.pass1_note: the pass-1 conical low-AR value (0.49) read the wrong curve; both passes are kept and the pixel pass is used

tm_x_1661_config1.geometry: configuration 1 with the ogive nose and low aspect ratio fins is the TN D-4013 short model (fineness ratio 18.2): ARCAS_COMPONENTS of wind-tunnel-models.ts; the conical (7.5 deg half-angle) and spherical (r = 2.907 cm) noses and the high aspect ratio fins (about 2.6 exposed) are recorded but not modelled

naca_rm_l8a05_fineness_7_87.source: NACA RM L8A05 (1948), free flight, fin-stabilised parabolic body of fineness ratio 7.87 (basic parabola of fineness ratio 10 cut at 61 in), model A, Mach 0.58 to 1.19; figure 8(a) (PDF page 24): total drag coefficient on the maximum frontal area; figure 6 (PDF page 21): Reynolds number on the body length 17e6 at M 0.62 to 55e6 at 1.19
naca_rm_l8a05_fineness_7_87.reference: coefficients on the maximum cross-section (d = 7.76 in); free flight: base included

cd_total_model_A.note: model A circles. Pass 1 was read from an 80 dpi contact-sheet thumbnail and is kept for the record but disagrees with the two full-resolution passes by up to 0.07 in the drag rise; the pixel pass (pass 2) is the value series and pass 3 (by eye from the unmarked 250 dpi render, after pass 2) is the check

geometry_inches.note: figure 1(a) (PDF page 9): profile Y = Ymax - 0.002577 X^2 with Ymax = 3.88 at station 38.8 (diameters at stations 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 38.8, 48, 56, 61: 0, 2.87, 5.08, 6.62, 7.52, 7.76, 7.35, 6.30, 5.15); three untapered fins swept 60 deg, circular-arc section t/c 0.10 normal to the leading edge, chord 4.625 normal to the leading edge (9.25 streamwise), tip radius 8.65, thickness 0.4625, wooden models; the fin trailing edge at the root is at the base
geometry_inches.modelling: nose = parabolic series K = 1, length 38.8, radius 3.88; boattail = unclipped parabolic transition K = 1 from 3.88 to 2.61 over 22.2 (the equation gives 2.61 at station 61 where the drawing lists 5.15/2 = 2.575); fins: root chord 9.25 (root leading edge at 51.75), tip chord 9.25, span 5.9 from the mean root radius 2.75, sweep 10.2, cross-section 'airfoil', count 3
